deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected German draft of an administrative report (Gutachten), written in Riemann's hand. It seems to be a passage from a joint opinion of Göttingen scholars to the Hanoverian authorities. The subject is whether Hanover should take part in the project proposed by General-Lieutenant Johann Jacob Baeyer: the 'Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung' of 1861-62, an international geodetic arc measurement.

Reconstructed argument, reading the surviving (uncancelled) text in order:
(1) The authors attach to their 'gehorsamster Bericht' (most obedient report) a discussion of the proposed undertaking. This discussion arose from their joint deliberation ('gemeinschaftliche Berathung'). They attach it as an appendix (Anlage) so that they can refer to the reasons developed there.
(2) The main sentence, assembled from the margin word 'Indem' and the later lines, reads roughly: 'Indem wir die Triangulirung Hannovers und ihre Verbindung mit den Dreiecksnetzen der Nachbarländer als im Wesentlichen vollendet betrachten, womit die wichtigste Grundlage gegeben ist, ... so glauben wir doch, daß hierdurch eine Mitwirkung bei dem vom General-Lieutenant Baeyer angeregten Unternehmen nicht ausgeschlossen ist.' In English: although they regard the Hanoverian triangulation and its connection to the networks of neighbouring countries as essentially complete, they believe Hanover's participation in Baeyer's project is not thereby excluded. The Hanoverian triangulation is Gauss's survey; the word 'gaußischen' was written and then struck.
(3) An alternative version says the Hanoverian triangulation itself should be regarded as concluded. It adds that one should wait to see whether, as noted in the appendix, Prussia still wishes a connection to the Hanoverian arc measurement.
(4) The last line is a heading for the next section: 'Das Unternehmen des General-Lieutenant Baeyer.'

There are no formulas, computations or mathematical arguments to restate. The mathematical content of the neighbouring pages (theta characteristics, binomial sums, the twin-prime prize question) does not continue here. This sheet is administrative scrap paper within the bundle.

results.what: Draft of an expert opinion on Hanover's participation in Baeyer's Central European arc measurement. It states that Gauss's Hanoverian triangulation, linked to neighbouring networks, is essentially complete, but that this does not exclude participation.
results.modern_name: Mitteleuropäische Gradmessung (precursor of the Internationale Erdmessung / IAG); history of geodesy
results.usually_credited_to: J. J. Baeyer (proposal 1861); Hanoverian triangulation by C. F. Gauss (1821-1844)

deep.surprise_reason: No mathematics. It is a minor biographical and administrative item: it shows Riemann drafting, presumably with Göttingen colleagues, an official opinion on Baeyer's geodetic project. This is mildly interesting to historians of geodesy and of Göttingen science policy, but carries no mathematical significance.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Wir haben uns[?]' is uncertain. The image may read 'Wir haben auf/nur unserem gehorsamsten Bericht'; a verb such as 'erlaubt' or 'beizufügen' governs the clause. The sense is 'we have attached to our most obedient report'.

The marginal word 'Indem' begins the main sentence ('Indem wir die Triangulirung Hannovers und ihre Verbindung mit den Dreiecksnetzen der Nachbarländer als im Wesentlichen vollendet betrachten, ...'). It is not a stray word.
'an die Hannoverschen[?] Gradmessung[?]' is probably 'an die Hannoversche Gradmessung' or 'an die Hannoverschen Messungen'.

In 'eine Vervollständigung[?] mit seinen Beobachtungen[?]' both words are doubtful. The image suggests something like 'eine Übereinstimmung mit seinen Ansichten/Annahmen', so the reading is unresolved.
The struck word before 'Dreiecksnetzen' is likely 'gaußischen', consistent with the struck 'Gaußischen Messungen in Hannover' above.
'Baeyer' (Johann Jacob Baeyer) is the correct reading of the general's name throughout.
